name: North Somerset

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme. A scheme proposed in 2016 for Central ward and part of Hillside in Weston-super-Mare was dropped after a legal challenge by landlords.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme found; national mandatory HMO licensing (five or more people forming two or more households) applies.

housing: Weston-super-Mare holds much of North Somerset's private rented stock, especially in the Victorian villas and terraces near the centre and seafront, many of them converted into flats. Clevedon has similar seaside period homes, while Portishead has grown fast with new-build estates and marina apartments. Nailsea, Worle and the villages are mainly owner-occupied family homes, and large new estates continue around Weston at Locking Castle and Haywood Village.
checkinTips: Converted flats in Weston's Victorian villas: photograph shared hallways, meter cupboards and fire doors, and note which keys open which doors.
Seafront homes in Weston and Clevedon: record salt marks and corrosion on window frames, railings and external doors.
Marina apartments in Portishead: note fob and key counts, parking bays and the condition of balconies.
New-build homes in Haywood Village and Portishead: photograph snagging marks, sealant around baths and the state of new turf and fences.
Stone cottages in the Mendip villages: photograph damp patches, chimneys, stoves and any oil tank or LPG supply.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to North Somerset Council's private housing team.
